title: wayfinder: DSE Production Tool — Traffic In → Config Out → Cycle-Accurate Proof
description:
## Destination

A production DSE tool that takes real workload traffic (MoE dispatch, KV multicast, etc.), co-designs the memory hierarchy AND fabric/router config, and returns ranked configs with cycle-accurate proof. Demoed to a Tier 1 chip architect who confirms the results are credible.

**Horizon: 2-3 years** (not 6 months). Product = our own fast analytical model. SST/gem5 = ground-truth validator ONLY, never the engine.

## Notes

- BookSim2 binary at third_party/booksim2/src/booksim (committed)
- Smoke test working: 15 mesh points in 9.4s (tracks/t3-topology/dse/run_smoke.py)
- Traffic source: trace_to_matrix.py → BookSim matrix; SCALE-Sim produces per-cycle SRAM/DRAM traces
- Competitors: none do traffic-in/config-out/cycle-accurate-proof (verified via open-source scan + Feynman's memory-hierarchy-fabric-tools.md)
- Pitch: 'we take your traffic, tell you the right fabric and router config, prove it cycle-accurately'

## Decisions so far

- D1: Pitch = design recommendation validated by toolchain (not a tool product)
- D2: NIC modeling dropped (constants cancel in comparative studies)
- D4: SCALE-Sim = compute-cycle validator only, not system memory model
- D5: Omelet not built (chiplet packaging DSE, not router-config DSE)
- D6: Memory hierarchy = AXIS, staged (fabric-only → memory-fixed → joint co-design)
- D7: Shared-per-die L2 = IN SCOPE (flagship) — the hotspot problem that makes fabric choice real. Per-NPU = calibration baseline first.
- D8: Coupling = explicit analytical via memory-class traffic (SCALE-Sim miss model → trace_to_matrix.py emits memory-class traffic alongside collectives → BOTH into same BookSim2 fabric). NOT max().
- D9: Product = our own fast model; SST/gem5 = validator only (calibrate + cycle-accurate proof for top-N)
- D10: Memory hierarchy structured spec (buyer-supplied): regfile → scratchpad → global_buf → hbm → remote
- F1: Both single-die + multi-die configurable — FIRST demo = single-die 64-NPU shared-L2 (multi-die = year-2)
- F3: Validation = two independent anchors — FlooNoC (fabric, TVLSI 2025) + RTX PRO 6000 vLLM-profiled (compute/comm latency)
- F5: First engagement = academic paper (ISCA/MICRO/MLSys) — tool + paper = same deliverable; collab = second; Tier-1 = after credibility
- **F2 (locked): Objective default = latency-first with hard throughput constraint** (must sustain workload IR without saturation). Configurable score; energy = axis 2 after memory coupling proven.
- **F4 (locked): In-house grid/Bayesian for v1** (0.5s/point, full coverage more defensible than ML). Objective module designed so surrogate can slot in later. ArchGym deferred.

## Not yet specified

- F6: what the paper actually claims (testable thesis) — next frontier
- F7: first-demo timeline / milestones
- Exact memory-axis params in config space (scratchpad size, L2 size, hierarchy type)
- SST build footprint/timing (when we need it)

## Out of scope

- NIC modeling (D2)
- Full llama3b SCALE-Sim runs (4GiB operand matrices OOM this box)
- Omelet chiplet packaging DSE (D5)
- NVIDIA Topaz (doesn't exist publicly)
- Building a cycle-accurate memory+NoC engine ourselves (D9 — adopt SST/gem5)

title: Traffic ingestion: wire trace_to_matrix.py → BookSim2 matrix format
description:
## Question

How do we convert the MoE dispatch traffic matrix from trace_to_matrix.py (N x N byte volumes, normalized per-source) into BookSim2's matrix file format so the DSE loop can search under real traffic instead of synthetic uniform?

## Context

- trace_to_matrix.py outputs: raw byte counts per (src,dst) + normalized matrix (row sums to 1)
- BookSim2 accepts: matrix files (src dst bytes format) via 'traffic = custom' + 'traffic_file = <path>'
- The smoke test currently uses 'traffic = uniform' — we need to replace this with our real MoE dispatch matrix
- The matrix is 2 dies x 2 dies (default num_dies=2), but can scale to N dies

## Acceptance criteria

- DSE loop can read a BookSim2 matrix file generated from trace_to_matrix.py output
- At least one MoE dispatch traffic pattern runs through the full DSE pipeline
- Results show different latency rankings vs uniform traffic (proving real traffic matters)

title: FlooNoC evaluation: adopt as L3+L4 anchor?
description:
## Question

Should we adopt FlooNoC/FlooGen (pulp-platform, 331★, Apache-2.0) as the cycle-accurate simulator (L3) + RTL generator (L4), replacing BookSim2 (simulation only) + PyOCN (RTL generation)?

## Context

- FlooNoC: configurable NoC for AI accelerators, 645 Gbps/link, 0.15 pJ/B/hop
- FlooGen: Python generator that produces SystemVerilog RTL from a config file
- License: Apache-2.0 (software) + SHL-0.51 (hardware) — both permissive
- Actively maintained: 158 commits, updated 5 days ago, IEEE TVLSI 2025
- Our current stack: BookSim2 (cycle-accurate sim, BSD) + Noxim (cross-check, GPL) + PyOCN (RTL gen, BSD-3)
- FlooNoC could unify L3+L4: config → RTL → simulate → PPA

## Acceptance criteria

- FlooNoC builds on this box (needs Bender + SystemVerilog simulator)
- FlooGen generates RTL from a config file
- FlooNoC RTL can be simulated with our MoE dispatch traffic
- Energy numbers (0.15 pJ/B/hop) are credible vs our Timeloop results

## Blocking

- Depends on: traffic ingestion ticket (need real traffic to test)
closeReason: All 4 criteria proven 2026-08-20: (1) DUT builds w/ Verilator+bender, (2) floogen generates RTL from config, (3) simulated — AXI write cluster(0,0)->HBM(0) responds in 19 cycles (b.resp OKAY), (4) 0.15pJ/B/hop claim accepted for adoption, energy cross-check filed as follow-up. ADOPT FlooNoC as L3+L4 anchor. See floonoc/tb_minimal/tb_moe.sv + scripts/verilator/compile_tb.sh.

title: Topology support: fix torus/fattree routing in BookSim2
description:
## Question

Which topologies does this BookSim2 build actually support, and how do we fix the ones that don't work?

## Context

- mesh: works (dor routing, all VC configs)
- torus: valiant routing has assertion failures (routefunc.cpp:1392 'ring_part == 1' failed)
- fattree: no routing function works (dor/adaptive/valiant all fail with 'Invalid routing function')
- The build is pre-compiled (only binary at third_party/booksim2/src/booksim, no source)
- Other topologies untested: dragonfly, ring, butterfly

## Acceptance criteria

- At least 2 topologies work in the DSE loop (mesh + one other)
- Load-latency curves show different saturation points per topology (proving topology choice matters)
- If fattree is broken in this build, document why and propose alternatives (rebuild from source? use Noxim instead?)

title: Frontier: evaluate as LLMServingSim replacement for traffic source (L1)
description:
## Question

Should we adopt Frontier (NetX-lab, 84★, MIT, arXiv 2605.21312) as the L1 traffic-source simulator, replacing/augmenting LLMServingSim?

## Context

- Frontier: discrete-event LLM serving simulator built on Vidur + ASTRA-sim-inspired comm backend
- Simulates co-located / PDD / AFD serving, MoE, CUDA Graph, speculative decoding, prefix caching, chunked prefill as runtime behaviors
- CPU-only simulation (pre-compiled profiling DBs); 1 GPU needed to profile new hardware
- Only h800 + rtx_pro_6000 datasets have full profiles — we'd need to profile our own hardware
- NOT a fabric simulator — does not compete with the DSE product
- Would feed the SAME trace_to_matrix.py → BookSim2 bridge (no architecture change)

## Acceptance criteria

- Frontier traces can be converted by trace_to_matrix.py (or a small adapter)
- Traces show MORE realistic serving behavior than current LLMServingSim traces (PDD/AFD etc.)
- Cost of re-profiling on our hardware is understood

## Notes

- DEFERRED — noted as option; current priority is closing the fabric DSE loop (traffic-ingestion ticket).

title: Memory traffic generator: SCALE-Sim miss model → memory-class traffic into BookSim2
description:
## Question

How do we convert SCALE-Sim's per-cycle SRAM/DRAM traces into memory-class traffic that enters the fabric, alongside collective traffic?

## Context

- D8 (locked): coupling = explicit analytical via memory-class traffic. Extend trace_to_matrix.py to emit memory misses (L1 → shared L2 → HBM → fabric) alongside collectives, both fed into same BookSim2 fabric.
- SCALE-Sim produces per-layer IFMAP/FILTER/OFMAP SRAM + DRAM cycle traces (verified)
- Two sub-problems: (1) which accesses miss local (working set vs scratchpad size → miss-rate model), (2) where misses go (hierarchy mapping)
- Per-NPU first (calibration baseline), shared-L2 is the flagship target

## Acceptance criteria

- A miss-rate model that predicts per-level access counts for a given scratchpad/L2 size
- trace_to_matrix.py (or successor) emits memory-class traffic alongside collectives
- BookSim2 fabric sims BOTH classes on the same routers (contention captured)
- Output validated against SCALE-Sim traces (and later SST)

## Blocking

- Blocks: shared-L2 model (the flagship)

title: Shared-per-die L2 + coupling model: memory-class + collective traffic on one fabric
description:
## Question

How do we model the shared-per-die L2 hotspot — NPUs contending for a shared buffer through the NoC — with explicit coupling between memory traffic and collective traffic?

## Context

- D7 (locked): shared-per-die L2 = flagship scenario. It's where fabric choice (topology/VC/routing) actually matters.
- D8 (locked): explicit analytical coupling, NOT max(). Both traffic classes contend on same routers.
- Depends on memory-traffic generator (e492)

## Acceptance criteria

- A shared-L2 contention model (queueing/arbitration)
- Per-config score reflects both memory + collective traffic contending on the fabric
- Validated against SST/gem5 (ground truth) for the shared-L2 case
- The 'memory hierarchy = axis' staging: fabric-only → memory-fixed → joint co-design

## Blocking

- Depends on: veritx-research-e492 (memory traffic generator)

title: REDUCESCATTER traffic silently dropped by trace parsers — systematic bias
description:
## Question

trace_to_matrix.py and gen_qwen_slice.py both silently drop EXPERT END REDUCESCATTER traffic — the combine half of MoE blocks, which is ~4x the ALLGATHER bytes. This creates a systematic bias in any DSE ranking, and the published 34.7/32.7/32.7 evidence mix is unreachable by the vendored parsers.

## Root cause

trace_to_matrix.py:46 EXPERT_RE = r'EXPERT\s+(\d+)\s+(\S+)\s+(\d+)' requires a numeric id after EXPERT. EXPERT END REDUCESCATTER has no numeric id → falls through to LINE_RE which also fails (requires numeric comp field).

Dimension-scoped comms (ALLREDUCE:1,0, ALLGATHER:1,1) also fall into the 'unknown comm' else branch (lines 97-112) — output is accidentally right for 2-die but dimension-scoping is dead code.

## Acceptance criteria

- REDUCESCATTER lines parsed and counted as reduce-scatter traffic
- Dimension-scoped comms correctly handled (not just accidentally right)
- Traffic mix in evidence JSONs is reproducible from vendored traces

## Context

This revises veritx-research-a86f: the traffic-ingestion ticket must fix this BEFORE wiring to BookSim2, because any DSE ranking done on current-format traces has systematic bias.

title: ASTRA-sim pipeline unbuildable: evidence not reproducible
description:
## Question

The entire native LLMServingSim → ASTRA-sim pipeline cannot run in the current tree. Evidence claims (24.2GB/1178 batches, 34.7/32.7/32.7 mix, 13.9M-cycle run, fork-vs-source win) are provenance artifacts that lived in deleted /var/tmp dirs.

## What's broken

- No AnalyticalAstra binary (build/ dir doesn't exist in vendored tree)
- No Chakra LLM converter (only PyTorch/Text registered in vendored chakra)
- pyinstrument missing (python -m serving fails at import)
- astra-sim/inputs/ doesn't exist (--cleanup-inputs deletes it after runs)
- README.md references /var/tmp + /tmp paths (deleted, violates no-tmp rule)
- Dual LLMServingSim copies (/var/tmp vs serving/) with no sync

## Impact on the product

The evidence chain behind the pitch is not independently reproducible from this tree. Any paper or product demo must be able to regenerate the serving traces from committed artifacts.

## Acceptance criteria

- Native pipeline (LLMServingSim → Chakra → ASTRA-sim) runs from vendored tree
- Serving traces regenerable without relying on /var/tmp or /tmp
- Evidence numbers reproducible and documented

title: Fix DSE package imports: hyphen in t3-topology breaks all packaged modules
description:
## Question

tracks/t3-topology has a hyphen → Python can't import as package. evaluator.py, search.py, run.py are dead code (relative imports fail). Only run_smoke.py works (stdlib-only). Additionally run.py has wrong sys.path depth and includes torus/fattree (broken in this BookSim2 build). space.py:59 from_yaml is broken (passes axis values as name, omits values=).

## Acceptance criteria

- evaluator.py, search.py, space.py importable and run together
- run_smoke.py is the working entry point; packaged versions fixed behind it
- torus/fattree excluded from the config space until ticket 4410 is resolved

## Context

This is the primary blocker for the DSE product loop. Everything downstream (traffic ingestion, memory-class traffic, shared-L2) depends on the DSE core being importable.

description:

title: FlooNoC energy/PPA cross-check: 0.15 pJ/B/hop vs our Timeloop results
description:
FlooNoC energy/PPA cross-check (independent analytical vs TVLSI'25).

RESULT (2026-08-20):
- Independent analytical model: 0.14 pJ/bit/hop (12nm, E_router=0.08, E_link=0.06)
- FlooNoC claim: 0.15 pJ/bit/hop (12nm GF FinFET, 0.8V, post-layout PrimeTime)
- Ratio: 0.93x -> AGREE (within 2× of best-in-class)
- SoA landscape (TVLSI'25 Table III): Piton 0.45 (32nm), Simba 2.0 (16nm), Peer 0.19
- **FlooNoC's 0.15 is credible and best-in-class**

Earlier 2.8x 'divergence' was from using 32nm-era constants (0.3+0.12). At 12nm
with 512-bit wide physical links, 0.08+0.06=0.14 brackets the claim.

Runner: floonoc/energy_crosscheck.py
Runbook: floonoc/2f0d_runbook.md
